solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disruption in current shift up to crew?

indicators.note: to shift things is to move them about, so the following letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager asks whether a disruptive change of rota should be left to the crew to decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day', but it is electric current; the shift is the anagram, not a work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A power cut is a stoppage of the electricity supply, literally a disruption in the flow of current.

clue.text: Tree loved by many becoming hollow?

indicators.note: something hollow has had its centre scooped out, so the middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A much-loved old tree is decaying and turning hollow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven-letter word loses its central U, the fourth of seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing deciduous tree of the genus Populus.

clue.text: Film director in farmer's boots showing no ego

indicators.note: showing none of something means it is missing, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: rubber wellington boots, standard farmyard footwear
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A humble film director turns up on set in muddy farm boots, with no airs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellies are wellington boots, rubber boots worn in mud; removing I leaves the surname of Orson Welles, director of Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the American actor and director behind Citizen Kane, so he is a film director.

clue.text: Dress old lady with part to play in performance

blocks.note: to rig out is to dress

explanation.surface: Costuming an elderly actress who has a role in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' looks theatrical but is the definition in its sense of a fuss or rigmarole; 'old lady' is slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, tiresome procedure, which is what a fuss or 'a real performance' means colloquially.

clue.text: Strict sergeant-major married, looking good with uniform on

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet
a sergeant-major is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A stern sergeant-major has just married and looks smart in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'with uniform on' puts U on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncompromising means unwilling to make concessions, so firmly strict.

clue.text: Recluse tailed a dreamy lover

indicators.note: to tail something is to cut off its end, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A shy recluse follows a daydreaming sweetheart about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreamy' points to Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, in which Hermia is one of the four young lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermia loves Lysander in A Midsummer Night's Dream, making her a lover from the Dream.

clue.text: A little licence, as editor became less severe

indicators.note: a little of the phrase means only a small part of its letters is taken

blocks.note: found across the end of licence, all of as and the start of editor

explanation.surface: An editor relaxed slightly by allowing a bit of leeway.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means lessened or relaxed, as pain or pressure does when it becomes less severe.

clue.text: Significant retreat northwards initiated by ally

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: An important military withdrawal to the north was begun by an allied force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initiated by ally' puts the ally first.
explanation.definitionFit: Material can mean relevant or significant, as in a material fact in a legal case.

clue.text: Back to bed possibly the right choice?

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: as in 'years back', meaning in the past

explanation.surface: Is going back to bed perhaps the wise decision?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like it signals a reversal, but here it means 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: A good bet is a wise option or likely winner, a choice worth backing.

clue.text: Respite from book about how fast an object travels

blocks.note: an object is a thing, and its speed is its pace

explanation.surface: Someone wants relief from reading a physics textbook about velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short pause or rest, giving time to recover.

clue.text: Easterly wind in photo of the ocean

indicators.note: an easterly comes from the east and so travels westward, right to left in an across answer
in places one piece inside another

explanation.surface: A picture of a sea storm shows an easterly blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easterly wind' reads as one weather phrase, but the first word only turns the second around.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelagic is the adjective for the open sea, as in pelagic fish living away from the shore.

clue.text: Is too much duck on king's dish?

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so zero

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether serving duck to royalty is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird, but in cricket a duck is a score of nothing; 'on' in an across clue means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Sphere with a period for rotation

indicators.note: something put up for rotation is turned round, so the phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: the indefinite article before a vowel

explanation.surface: A globe spinning over a set time sounds like astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sphere' looks like a ball, but here it means a field of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a field of activity, as in the political arena, which is also what a sphere means.

clue.text: Wound Romeo in despicable act

indicators.note: Romeo placed in the act means it is set inside that word

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo is stabbed in a cowardly attack, as in a Shakespearean tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, as a river winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound (rhymes with sound) means twisted and turned, the same as meandered.

clue.text: The press in favour of US almost taking lead in Ukraine

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter
taking means swallowing something into the middle
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

explanation.surface: American newspapers are supporting the US position on Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is a traditional name for journalism and the news media, seen as a power alongside the others in a state.

clue.text: One believes in magic fake satin pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered

explanation.surface: A conjurer's trousers made of imitation satin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, which works as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamanist follows shamanism, a belief in spirits that a shaman reaches through magic and ritual.

clue.text: Fred spread diamonds with highest card on top, showing a flush

indicators.note: spread out means scattered, so the name's letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A poker player called Fred lays out diamonds topped by an ace to show a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on top' puts the ace above the diamonds. A flush in poker is five cards of one suit, but here it is a blush.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-faced describes someone blushing, and a flush is a reddening of the face.

clue.text: Order some naan with everybody doing likewise

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are set in a new sequence

explanation.surface: At a curry house everyone at the table copies the first person and asks for naan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a restaurant request; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As one man is an idiom meaning all together, in unison, everyone acting the same way.

clue.text: Reshuffle in See mandatory when Pope Francis died

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges positions, so the letters inside are put in a new order

explanation.surface: After a pope's death, a reshuffle in the Holy See becomes unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: The See is the Holy See, the papal government; the surface fits the topic exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope Francis died on 21 April 2025, the day after Easter Sunday, which was Easter Monday.

clue.text: Boat old boy capsized after training

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down answer the words are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor overturned his boat after a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After training' puts PE first.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by pedals, common at seaside resorts.

clue.text: Run out of clothes?

blocks.note: surface reading: to have nothing clean left to wear
setter's reading: to dash about in public with no clothes on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out of' reads as 'have none left'; instead it is running while out of your clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, often at a sports event.

clue.text: Last contestants heard better quality of Hungarian pianist

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: finer means better, and Franz Liszt was the Hungarian pianist

explanation.surface: A music critic praises the superior tone of a Hungarian pianist's recital.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where finer sounds like final.
explanation.definitionFit: Finalists are the contestants who remain for the final round of a competition.

clue.text: Fire bricks with studs across the front of them

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
lying across something means spanning it, so the bricks enclose the letter

blocks.note: the toy building bricks, which have studs on top
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a fireplace with studded bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames, but it means dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone go is a euphemism for dismissing them, the same as firing them.

clue.text: Infiltrator maybe not evacuated on time

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: the word with its inside removed

explanation.surface: A suspected spy may not have been cleared out in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuated' empties a word of its middle; 'on' in an across clue means placed after the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An infiltrator is one kind of agent, a spy sent into an enemy organisation; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Sporting Pom getting century after century

definitions.text: Sporting Pom getting century after century

indicators.note: sporting can mean playing about, so the short word's letters frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: An English sportsman piles up hundred after hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Denis Compton, English cricketer and footballer who scored over a hundred first-class centuries; Pom is Australian slang for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Compton was a celebrated English all-round sportsman whose batting yielded many cricket centuries.

clue.text: Someone annoying had to cause trouble

blocks.note: British slang for an irritating person; with someone, 'an annoying someone'
to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: An irritating person was obliged to stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Git is mild British slang for an unpleasant or annoying person.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up unrest or campaign disruptively, which is causing trouble.

clue.text: Scottish cheese is greyish- brown — cut bits off?

explanation.surface: Someone finds a Scottish cheese discoloured and wonders about trimming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunlop is a mild hard cheese from Ayrshire in Scotland, similar to cheddar.

clue.text: Send a surprising SMS back to shock model

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: to text someone the startling word boo

explanation.surface: Someone sends a startling message in reply to frighten a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model but is the adjective meaning exemplary; SMS is a mobile-phone text message.
explanation.definitionFit: Textbook as an adjective means exemplary or ideal, like a model example.
